title: The Share of the Unearned Premium a Given-Up Plan Returns
content:
The share of the unearned premium a Pass and Trip Protection plan returns when it is given up turns on the
plan's refund basis, on whether any payout stands on it for the season, and on how much of its term has run.

| The plan and its season | The share returned |
| --- | --- |
| The plan returns premium on a pro rata basis, no payout stands on it for the season, and it is given up after the first half of its term has run | The whole of the unearned premium |
| The plan returns premium on a pro rata basis, no payout stands on it for the season, and it is given up inside the first half of its term | 90.00 per cent of the unearned premium |
| Any other case | Nothing |

**Reading the schedule.** Both of the first two rows are compound and require the plan to return premium on a
pro rata basis and to carry no payout at all for the season. Between them the question is only how much of the
term has run, measured from the day cover began to the day the plan is given up, against the days from the day
cover began to the day cover is due to end: more than half falls on the first row, half or less on the second.
The last row takes everything else, a plan on which a payout stands for the season included, since the cover
has already answered for itself; so does a plan whose refund basis is no refund at all.

**Worked figures (hypothetical inputs).** A plan on a pro rata basis with no payout for the season, given up
with three fifths of its term run, returns the whole of an unearned premium of 80.00 USD, which is 80.00 USD.
The same plan given up with a quarter of its term run returns 90.00 per cent of it, which is 72.00 USD. The
same plan with one payout standing for the season returns nothing at all.
